title: Why Australia went to war
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:18Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 says reuse his-australians-enlisted, so to the Opus match check, as every reuse is
2026-11-20T12:25:51Z confirm: Claude Opus 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point 'Why Australians enlisted' teaches the same idea (loyalty to Britain, adventure, pay and social pressure as reasons for AIF enlistment) at a suitable Year 9 depth, and its questions and content fit the new point and NSW course without change.

confirm.reason: The bank point covers only why individual men enlisted; the new point also needs to teach why Australia itself entered the war in 1914 as part of the British Empire, and adding that would be a new step rather than a small change.

draft.title: Why Australia went to war
card: In 1914 Australia was a self-governing nation within the British Empire, but Britain still controlled its foreign policy. When Britain declared war on Germany in August 1914, Australia was at war too.
Many Australians felt strong ties to Britain. They saw it as the mother country and believed they should defend the Empire.
Australia's government promised to send an all-volunteer force. Thousands of men enlisted in 1914.
Men had different reasons for enlisting. Some felt loyal to Britain, some wanted adventure and travel, and some wanted the regular pay.
draft.remember: Being part of the Empire put Australia into the war, and men chose to enlist for many reasons.

a.q: Why was Australia at war as soon as Britain declared war in 1914?
opts: It was part of the British Empire, which Britain led
It had signed a treaty with Germany's enemies in 1913
Its own parliament had voted to attack Germany first
Germany had invaded Australian territory that week
a.why: Britain controlled Australia's foreign policy as head of the Empire, so its declaration took Australia to war too. Australia's parliament did not start the war itself.
a.clue: Think about who controlled foreign policy.

b.q: In 1914 Tom, a farm worker in Wagga Wagga, enlists because he has never left New South Wales and wants to see the world. Which reason for enlisting does this show?
b.why: Tom wants to travel and see new places, which is the desire for adventure. Loyalty to Britain is a tempting answer, but nothing in his reasons mentions the Empire.
b.clue: What does Tom say he wants to do?

a.best: It was part of the British Empire, which Britain led

check.summary: No problems found. The facts about the Empire, foreign policy and the volunteer force are accurate, and both questions have one clear right answer.
